analysis.title: GS TWIG Notes: This Week in Global Research - October 16, 2026
key_insights: Goldman's Christian Mueller-Glissmann raises equities to Overweight on a 3-month basis and bonds to Overweight on a 12-month basis. Equity valuations have de-rated despite robust earnings growth, and higher carry, better return asymmetry and lower expected inflation support more normal strategic bond allocations. Tactical caution on duration remains because of higher yields, fiscal concerns, AI-related capital competition and inflation uncertainty.

Treasury yields have risen this year because the Fed moved from cutting to hiking, US-Iran War inflation risks, receding labor stress, a better global growth outlook and higher yields outside the US (Will Marshall).

Moody's Mark Zandi sees one-in-three odds of the economy going off the rails because of the rate move already seen, while others are less concerned (Allison Nathan, Top of Mind). Key watch item is whether the leveraged, interconnected AI investment boom can withstand higher rates.

Johan Allen estimates the average developed market economy loses 0.6% of GDP within a year of a 100bp rise in rates, through lower housing investment, consumer spending and business investment, plus a heavier interest burden on government debt.
In credit, Sara Grut recommends seeking higher yields with limited duration risk: lean into USD over EUR and BBBs over AAs and As.

Related GS notes cited: Warsh did not address the October FOMC meeting but said the world has broadly conformed to the Fed's expectations since the last meeting; core CPI came in above expectations with September core PCE estimated at 0.32%; mortgage rates reached 7.4%, called an affordability headwind, not a housing market breaker.

In China, almost $5tn of market cap has been created by AI-related public equities through price gains and IPOs in under two years (Kinger Lau). GS favors Chinese AI export leaders, select domestic AI champions and a refreshed China Select AI Portfolio.

Jessica Rindels and David Mericle estimate AI demand is boosting US core PCE by about 45bps, through pricier hardware and software and higher power and industrial metals costs. They think the AI inflation impulse is near its peak.

USD project finance issuance has already tripled the total raised in 2025 as neoclouds and hyperscalers tap debt markets (Amanda Lynam). Funding costs have risen for some issuers but not all, and GS sees upside to next year's issuance. Focus is on careful underwriting.
UK GDP growth is accelerating this year on a resilient consumer and corporate sector, global activity and weather, not AI (James Moberly).
Music: GS raises its music industry growth forecast to a +5.8% 2025-35E CAGR on subscription pricing, better ad-supported economics and GenAI. Favored names: SPOT, GOOGL, TME, SONY, LYV, HYBE, NTES.

MENA banks: higher-for-longer rates will affect the four GCC systems unevenly, creating dispersion larger than differences in credit quality, capital or efficiency (Kazim Andac). Singapore real estate: the current rate hike cycle is shorter and shallower, so the sector correction looks overdone (Xuan Tan).
Animal Health: Matt Dellatorre initiates at Buy on ELAN and IDXX and Neutral on ZTS, citing competition and a post-COVID hangover.

Memory: Jim Schneider sees High-Bandwidth Flash reaching a $40-$150B TAM by 2030E and lowering costs by about 30%. BT substrate TAM is expected to grow at a 32% 2026-28E CAGR, with the supply/demand gap widening to 11%/14% in 2027/28E from 1% in 2026E.
ASML and TSMC both said AI demand is still outpacing supply even as they add capacity.

HVAC: Joe Ritchie upgrades TT to Buy and downgrades LII and CARR to Neutral, as data center demand drives Applied HVAC backlog while competition pressures Resi HVAC pricing. ANZ data centers face a 0.7GW supply shortfall by 2030E.
Defense: Noah Poponak prefers defense tech over legacy defense for growth, margin expansion and better ability to run commercial models.
LNG: GS sees a tight near-term global LNG supply/demand balance that could weaken later this decade as supply growth outpaces demand growth.

Oil shipping: crude freight costs have risen sharply this year, driving wide regional divergence in delivered oil and a return to regional trading. Batteries: GS is not yet calling a cyclical bottom; favors LG Chem, LGES and CATL.

China logistics: Ronald Keung is incrementally cautious on profit growth because of slowing online consumption and persistent overcapacity. African gold miners: Matt Greene initiates with strong margins, low leverage and attractive free cash flow; Buy AGA and EDV.
Single-stock calls: ZETA up to Buy, Technip Energies upgrade to Buy, IWG initiate at Buy, GXO up to Buy, BCP (Portuguese bank) upgrade to Buy.
ESMO conference next week: GS previews key cancer data for MRK, MRNA and SMMT (Phase 3 ivonescimab).
